title: Pine tool tote
subtitle: A simple carrying box for hand tools
excerpt: A pine tool tote: 42 cm by 18 cm by 15 cm deep, with a central handle rail that rises above the sides. The open-top box carries chisels, a marking gauge, and a tenon saw without needing a lid. Cut from a single length of prepared pine board; assembled with screws.
sourceNotes: Traditional British workshop joinery pattern; open-top tool tote construction documented in Charles Hayward, Woodwork Joints (1950 ed.).

glossaryTerms.definition: Timber dried to equilibrium moisture content for indoor use. Dimensionally stable; does not shrink after working.
Timber that has been planed smooth and to a consistent thickness on all four faces. Sold by merchants as PAR (planed all round). Ready to mark and cut without further surfacing.

content.text: A pine tool tote in
seasoned wood
: 42 cm by 18 cm by 15 cm deep, with a 3 cm central handle rail. All parts cut from one length of
prepared timber
(PAR pine, 18 mm thick). The handle rail runs between the two short ends; the two long sides slot against the ends and the base sits underneath. Assembled with 40 mm wood screws.
Before you start cutting.
Tenon saw: use a bench hook or vice to hold the workpiece. Never grip the timber with your free hand directly in the saw's path.
Cordless drill: clamp the workpiece before drilling. The drill bit can snag on breakthrough; keep your hand clear of the underside.
First aid: a styptic pencil, gauze, and a clean dressing should be within reach. Firm pressure on a saw cut, elevate, dress. A cut that shows fat or will not close goes to A&E.
Wood

One length of 18 mm PAR pine or redwood, 140 mm wide, 1.8 m long. From this single length you cut: two long sides (42 cm), two short ends (18 cm), one base (42 cm), and one handle rail (42 cm, 60 mm wide ripped from the edge). PAR timber is sold at all DIY merchants. Check it is straight and free of large knots at the ends.
Cutting list
2 long sides: 420 mm by 150 mm by 18 mm.
2 short ends: 180 mm by 150 mm by 18 mm.
1 base: 420 mm by 180 mm by 18 mm.
1 handle rail: 420 mm by 60 mm by 18 mm.
Method
Step 1: Mark and saw the parts

Mark each piece with the marking gauge and try square. Saw to the line with the tenon saw, keeping cuts vertical. Check each piece against the try square after sawing; a small error at this stage multiplies at assembly. The handle rail is narrower than the board; rip it from one long edge with the tenon saw following a marked gauge line.
Step 2: Sand all faces

Sand all faces and edges with 240-grit on the sanding block, then 320-grit. Remove saw marks on the end grain faces. Break the sharp arris on every edge with one or two strokes of 240-grit paper; a softened edge resists splitting in use.
Step 3: Drill the handle arch (optional)

Mark two finger holes in the handle rail: 90 mm from each end, centred on the rail width. Drill a 30 mm hole at each mark (hole-saw or spade bit). Join the two holes with two straight saw cuts to make an arch opening 30 mm tall by 150 mm wide. Sand the arch edges smooth.
Step 4: Assemble with screws

Fix the two short ends to the base first. Drill two 4 mm pilot holes through the base into the end face of each short piece. Drive 40 mm screws. Then fix the two long sides: pilot and screw through the sides into the short ends (two screws per corner). Finally, fit the handle rail: stand it on edge between the two short ends, centred, and screw through each short end into the handle rail (two screws per end).
Finishing

Two coats of danish oil, wiped on with a cloth and left for twenty minutes before wiping dry. The second coat goes on after four hours. Danish oil is a penetrating finish; it does not build up on the surface. The tote will darken slightly to a honey colour. Leave overnight before loading with tools.

attrs.symptom: The box is racked (out of square)
attrs.cause: One or more parts were not cut square, or the screws pulled the assembly out of true.
attrs.fix: Check each part with the try square before assembly. Clamp the assembly square while the screws go in. If the box is already assembled and racked, loosen the screws slightly, clamp square, and re-drive.

attrs.symptom: The screw head splits the timber at the end grain
attrs.cause: No pilot hole, or pilot hole too small.
attrs.fix: Pre-drill a 4 mm pilot hole 5 mm from the end before driving the screw. End grain in pine splits easily under screw pressure without a pilot.
